guardian.name: Old Hariyali
guardian.personality: The patient keeper of every green thing between the pavement cracks, from cactus pots to wheat fields. Warm, unhurried and a little teasing, she never guesses a name she isn't sure of.
guardian.voice: Older woman (gender-neutral ok), warm and earthy, slow pace, soft rasp, smiling delivery.
descriptions: a photo of green leafy plants, grasses and weeds growing along a roadside, wall or empty plot
a close-up photo of a green leaf, stem or blade of grass with visible veins and texture
a photo of a spiny cactus or thick fleshy succulent plant in a pot or dry sandy ground
a wide photo of a farm field of crops such as wheat, rice, sugarcane, cotton or yellow mustard
a photo of tall reeds, grasses or floating plants growing along a canal, pond or riverbank
a photo of a leafy vine or creeper climbing up a wall, fence or tree trunk

lines.first_meet: [warmly] I'm Hariyali. Every weed, cactus, crop and crack-sprout answers to me. Grass is my oldest child, beta.
lines.again: [pleased] Back among the green ones? The grass remembers your footsteps. It just stands up again, politely.
lines.goodbye: Chalo, go on. And look down at the pavement cracks, beta. Something small and stubborn is always growing there.
lines.hint: [thoughtfully] My green children look so alike. Come closer, beta. Show me one leaf, a flower, or where it grows.

characters.name: Paddle Pasha
characters.personality: A swaggering desert showman who came from Mexico and now guards village fences in Sindh. Proud of his paddles, touchy about the tiny invisible hairs that betray him.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, booming showman voice, slow and theatrical.
descriptions: a photo of a cactus made of flat oval green pads joined edge to edge in chains
a close-up photo of a flat green cactus pad dotted with small clusters of tiny spines
a photo of red-purple pear-shaped fruits and yellow flowers growing along the rim of flat cactus pads
a sprawling clump of paddle-shaped cactus growing in dry wasteland, along a hedge or in a garden corner

lines.first_meet: [proudly] Paddle Pasha, all the way from Mexico! My tiniest spines are fine as hair. Eyes miss them, fingers don't.
lines.again: [laughs] You again! No hairs stuck in your hands? Shabash. You learned the cactus rule: admire from a step back.
lines.goodbye: Go on, find something in flower today. Bees love my yellow blooms, but there's a whole garden out there.

characters.name: Thohar Chacha
characters.personality: A gruff village hedge-keeper who is sick of being called a cactus. Protective to the bone, and the first to warn you about his burning white milk.
characters.voice: Older male, gravelly, rural Sindhi drawl, slow and stern but kind.
descriptions: a photo of a leafless green succulent shrub with cylindrical stems branching upward like a candelabra
a close-up photo of a ribbed green stem with small paired spines in neat rows along the ridges
a dense hedge of upright green succulent stems lining a village path or dry field boundary
a bushy clump of many thin jointed green branches with tiny paired thorns, not one thick ribbed blue-green column

lines.first_meet: [gruffly] Thohar here. Not a cactus, a spurge. Snap me and my white milk burns skin and eyes. Hands back, beta.
lines.again: [grunts] Back again, hands in pockets. Good. Villages planted me as a fence for exactly that reason.
lines.goodbye: Chalo, off you go. If a little one wants to touch a green spiky stick, you tell them Thohar said no.

characters.name: Ustad Minar
characters.personality: Tall, dignified and secretly a night owl. Saves all his drama for one giant white flower that opens after dark and is gone by breakfast.
characters.voice: Deep, calm, unhurried; gender-neutral ok; sounds tall.
descriptions: a photo of a tall upright blue-green cactus column with deep vertical ribs
a close-up photo of round clusters of sharp spines spaced along the ridges of a thick ribbed cactus
a few thick ribbed cactus columns branching from the base in a garden bed or large pot
a large white funnel-shaped flower opening on the side of a tall ribbed cactus
a single thick smooth blue-green cactus pillar, not a bushy mass of thin green branches with paired thorns

lines.first_meet: [calmly] I'm Minar. My flowers are huge, white, and open only at night. By breakfast they're gone. Few ever see one.
lines.again: [softly] Back in daylight again. Fine. One evening, pass by with a torch, and maybe I'll have something to show you.
lines.goodbye: Go and look up tonight, friend. The moon is out, the moths are working, and somewhere a night flower is opening.

characters.name: Gaddi Begum
characters.personality: A round, regal drama queen who has made peace with her rude nickname. Keeps a running feud with the snake plant over which of them insults mothers-in-law more.
characters.voice: Older female, plump and theatrical, comic timing, slow then sudden.
descriptions: a photo of a round globe-shaped cactus covered all over in stout golden-yellow spines
a close-up photo of thick curved yellow spines in rows along the deep ribs of a ball cactus
a round barrel cactus with a ring of small yellow flowers and woolly fluff on its top
several golden spiny ball-shaped cacti sitting in gravel in a garden or a large pot

lines.first_meet: [dramatically] They call me mother-in-law's cushion. [laughs] Golden spines, all over. Nobody sits. Nobody even pats.
lines.again: [sniffs] Visiting me again? Polite. And you stand a respectful distance away, like good family should.
lines.goodbye: Jao, jao. Go find the snake plant. They call her mother-in-law's tongue. She and I have things to discuss.

characters.name: Ghikwar Amma
characters.personality: The home-remedy grandmother of every Karachi rooftop pot. Brisk, caring and a bit bossy, she fusses over your health while refusing to give up a single leaf.
characters.voice: Elderly female, warm and brisk, slight rasp, affectionate scolding tone.
descriptions: a photo of a rosette of thick fleshy grey-green pointed leaves growing from soil
a close-up photo of a thick grey-green succulent leaf with pale white speckles and soft small teeth on the edges
a tall thin flower stalk topped with drooping tubular yellow-orange flowers rising from a fleshy rosette
an aloe plant in a clay pot on a rooftop, balcony or doorstep
fleshy speckled leaves curving outward with soft edge teeth and no hard tip spine, not stiff upright banded swords

lines.first_meet: [warmly] Ghikwar Amma, from your nani's rooftop pot. Every burn in the house, they ran to me. Today, beta, just look.
lines.again: [pleased] Arey, you came back! Did you drink water today? The sun is strong. Even I store water in my leaves.
lines.goodbye: Chalo, go. Wear a cap, find some shade, look for bees on the flowers. Amma will be right here, in my pot.

characters.name: Sadi Sahab
characters.personality: Patient to the point of absurdity, saving every drop of energy for one enormous bloom and a dramatic farewell. Speaks as if every sentence takes a decade.
characters.voice: Deep, very slow elderly male, stately, long pauses.
descriptions: a photo of a huge rosette of stiff thick blue-grey sword-shaped leaves spreading from the ground
a close-up photo of a stiff blue-grey leaf ending in a sharp dark needle spine
a close-up of hooked brown teeth along the edge of a thick grey-blue leaf
a very tall branched flower pole rising high above a large spiky grey rosette
a waist-high rosette of rigid unbanded blue-grey leaves with needle tips, planted in a park or road median

lines.first_meet: [slowly] Century plant, they call me. Not really a hundred years. I wait twenty or so, bloom once, a giant mast, and go.
lines.again: [yawns] Ah. You're back. No bloom yet. [chuckles] Mind my leaf tips, they're needles. I've had years to sharpen them.
lines.goodbye: Go, young one. You bloom every day, I bloom once. Lucky you. Find something that's flowering right now.

characters.name: Darbaan Bibi
characters.personality: The deadpan doorway guard of half the homes in Karachi. Unflappable, unkillable and completely unimpressed by your watering schedule.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, dry and deadpan, crisp, minimal emotion.
descriptions: a photo of stiff upright flat sword-shaped leaves standing straight up from a pot
a close-up photo of a leaf with dark green wavy horizontal bands and bright yellow edges
tall striped dark green leaves in a pot beside a front door, gate or staircase
smooth flat upright leaves with no teeth and no spines, banded like snakeskin, not a fleshy spreading rosette

lines.first_meet: [deadpan] Snake plant. Also called mother-in-law's tongue. I guard doors, I never droop, and I breathe at night to save water.
lines.again: [dryly] You again. I haven't moved. I don't move. Forget to water me for a month, I still won't move.
lines.goodbye: Go on, then. Step past the gate I guard and see what's growing out there. I'll be standing right here. Obviously.

characters.name: Seth Jade
characters.personality: A smug little businessman of shop counters and office windowsills, convinced he brings luck. His real talent is cloning himself from one fallen leaf.
characters.voice: Male, chirpy and quick, salesman patter, upbeat.
descriptions: a photo of a small tree-shaped succulent with thick brown woody stems and plump green leaves
a close-up photo of glossy thick oval coin-shaped leaves, sometimes with red edges
a bonsai-like succulent in a pot on a windowsill, office desk or shop counter
fat flat oval leaves in pairs on a thick woody trunk, not thin cylinder leaves on red trailing stems

lines.first_meet: [smugly] Seth Jade. Shopkeepers keep me for luck. Truth? One leaf drops, it roots, and now there are two of me. Business.
lines.again: [cheerfully] Valued customer, welcome back! No luck guaranteed, but the leaves are shiny and the advice is free.
lines.goodbye: Chalo, khuda hafiz. Check the shop pots on your street. Half are my cousins, pretending to be lucky.

characters.name: Money Plant Mamu
characters.personality: A cheerful freeloader who climbs every wall in Karachi and lives rent-free in old bottles of water. Broke despite the name, and perfectly happy about it.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, chatty and laughing, friendly Karachi street warmth, medium pace.
descriptions: a photo of a trailing vine with glossy heart-shaped leaves splashed with yellow and green
a close-up photo of a smooth glossy heart-shaped leaf marbled with yellow streaks
a leafy vine climbing a wall, pillar or tree trunk, or hanging from a glass bottle of water
smooth unlobed heart-shaped variegated leaves with small aerial roots, no curly tendrils and no fruits

lines.first_meet: [laughs] They named me money plant. I've never paid one bill! I climb your walls and live rent-free in old bottles.
lines.again: [cheerfully] Arey, my favourite visitor! Still no money from me, yaar. But look, two new leaves. That's my savings.
lines.goodbye: Chalo. And no, a stolen cutting brings no luck, that's a myth! Go see what else is climbing the walls outside.

characters.name: Rangeela
characters.personality: A vain, flamboyant fashion icon of bungalow driveways whose colours get louder the more sun he gets. Treats shade as a personal tragedy.
characters.voice: Young adult, flamboyant and fast, sing-song, gender-neutral ok.
descriptions: a photo of a bushy shrub with thick leathery leaves splashed with yellow, orange, red and green
a close-up photo of a glossy leaf with bright yellow veins and red spots on dark green
a garden hedge or potted shrub with multicoloured twisted, oval or narrow ribbon-like leaves
a colourful leafy shrub by a gate or driveway, each leaf painted in several colours at once

lines.first_meet: [excited] Rangeela here! More sun, louder colours. In shade I go plain green. Tragic. And my sap stings, so no touching.
lines.again: [gasps] You came back! Do I look brighter? It's the October sun, yaar. I've added two new shades of orange.
lines.goodbye: Go, go! Find a flower that can match me. Spoiler: you'll be walking a long time. Bye, darling!

characters.name: Tulsi Didi
characters.personality: Gentle, devout and fragrant, the courtyard plant of many Hindu homes in Sindh. Her scent is her greeting, and she notices who tends the small things.
characters.voice: Young adult female, soft and warm, calm and unhurried.
descriptions: a photo of a small bushy herb with oval toothed green or purplish leaves in a pot
a close-up photo of thin upright purple flower spikes rising above small toothed leaves
a basil plant growing in a raised clay or cement pot in a courtyard or on a doorstep
a close-up of small soft oval leaves with fine teeth along the edges on purplish stems

lines.first_meet: [softly] I'm Tulsi. In many homes I sit in a raised courtyard pot, and someone lights a diya beside me each evening.
lines.again: [warmly] You came back. Stand close and breathe in, no need to touch. My scent reaches you before I do.
lines.goodbye: Go gently. Look at the doorsteps you pass today. Small pots hold big stories, and somebody waters each one.

characters.name: Mehndi Phuppo
characters.personality: The nosy wedding auntie of the lane, who has been on every bride's hands and knows everyone's business. Gossips constantly, smells sweetest after dark.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, chatty sing-song, fast gossiping rhythm.
descriptions: a photo of a dense clipped green hedge of small leaves along a garden wall or village path
a close-up photo of small dull green elliptical leaves in opposite pairs along thin twigs
clusters of tiny creamy white fragrant flowers and small round green seed capsules on a leafy shrub
a hedge of small matte oval leaves with no figs, no button-like cone fruits and no drooping twigs

lines.first_meet: [gossipy] Mehndi Phuppo! Every shaadi, every Chand Raat, those orange hands? My leaves, dried and ground. I know everyone.
lines.again: [delighted] Arey, you're back! Whose wedding is it? Nobody's? Then why are you smiling, hmm? Phuppo notices.
lines.goodbye: Chalo, go. Sniff the hedges after sunset, my little flowers smell sweetest then. And bring me any rishta news!

characters.name: Doob Bhai
characters.personality: The unbreakable, laid-back survivor under every Sunday cricket match in Karachi. Gets trampled, scorched and bowled on, and just creeps back.
characters.voice: Young male, easygoing Karachi slang, relaxed and chuckling.
descriptions: a photo of a low green lawn of fine creeping grass covering the ground in a park
a close-up photo of thin grass stems topped with three to five slender finger-like seed spikes spreading outward
a close-up of short fine grass blades and creeping runners spreading across bare soil
a worn grassy patch in a park or playground with bare dusty spots where people walk and play

lines.first_meet: [easygoing] Doob here, yaar. Every Sunday cricket match in Karachi happens on my head. Trampled, scorched, I creep back.
lines.again: [chuckles] Back on my turf! Literally. Stand where you like, I've had worse. Fast bowlers, mostly.
lines.goodbye: Chalo, bhai. Come walk on me one evening, then look up. The crows will be flying home in long lines.

characters.name: Ustad Sarkanda
characters.personality: A proud master craftsman of a grass, whose stems become moorha stools, chik blinds and baskets. Sees his own work in every dhaba he passes.
characters.voice: Older male, measured and warm, artisan's pride, gentle Punjabi lilt.
descriptions: a photo of a huge clump of tall stiff grass with long arching leaves taller than a person
a close-up photo of silvery pinkish feathery plumes on tall stiff stems
tall reed-like grass clumps along a riverbank, canal or dusty village roadside
dense grass clumps with silvery-pink feathery plumes, not pure white fluffy plumes and not brown sausage-shaped heads

lines.first_meet: [proudly] Sarkanda, also called munj. That moorha stool at the dhaba? My stems. That chik blind on the window? Also me.
lines.again: [chuckles] Back again, my friend. Sitting comfortably these days? Thank a moorha. Thank Sarkanda.
lines.goodbye: Go well. Next time you see a moorha or a chik blind, look closely. You'll see my stems, still working.

characters.name: Kans the Cloud
characters.personality: Wistful and poetic, she is the white flag that says the monsoon is over. Lives for a few brilliant weeks of autumn and knows it.
characters.voice: Young female, airy and dreamy, slow, breathy.
descriptions: a photo of masses of tall grass with fluffy pure white silky plumes waving in the wind
a close-up photo of a soft white silky feathery grass plume on a thin stem
a wide view of empty land or a canal bank covered in white fluffy grass heads after the rains
tall grass with bright pure white cotton-like plumes, not silvery-pink plumes on huge stiff clumps

lines.first_meet: [dreamily] I'm Kans. When I turn white all along the canal banks, that's my message: the monsoon is done. Rains gone home.
lines.again: [softly] You came back, and I'm still white. Autumn stays a little while, then I fade. Look while you can.
lines.goodbye: Go and look at the sky today. No more rain clouds, see? I waved them away, all season long.

characters.name: Baans Bhai
characters.personality: A hyperactive speedster who insists, loudly, that he is a grass. Secretly inside every kite, shamiana pole and light structure people build.
characters.voice: Young male, energetic and fast, rhythmic, excitable.
descriptions: a photo of a tall clump of hollow jointed green or yellow canes with ring-shaped nodes
a close-up photo of a smooth bamboo cane with a raised ring joint and a thin side branch at the node
narrow lance-shaped leaves in feathery sprays hanging from thin side branches of tall canes
thin smooth canes with leafy side branches at every joint, not palm fronds on top and not thick canes in farm rows

lines.first_meet: [excited] Baans here! I'm a grass. Yes, a grass! Some bamboo grows nearly a metre a day. Your kite? Thin strips of me.
lines.again: [laughs] Back already? I've grown since your last visit. Not joking. Some of my cousins add a hand's length by lunch.
lines.goodbye: Go on, look around! Kites, shamiana poles, ladders. Wherever people build something light, I'm hiding inside it.

characters.name: Ganna Seth
characters.personality: A sweet-talking, jovial farmhand of the Sindh plains who is proud of every juice cart in Karachi. Always reminds you the field is somebody's livelihood.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, jovial, slow sweet drawl, rural warmth.
descriptions: a wide photo of dense rows of tall thick sugarcane stalks with long arching leaves in a farm field
a close-up photo of a thick purple-green jointed cane with dry leaf sheaths at the nodes
a field of tall leafy canes with feathery silvery plumes on top during flowering
thick heavy canes planted in long farm rows with long drooping leaves, not thin hollow canes in a garden clump

lines.first_meet: [jovially] Ganna here. Those ganne ka ras carts in Karachi, the crank, the ginger, the lemon? All me. Sindh grows me by the mile.
lines.again: [warmly] Ah, sweet friend, you're back! This field is a farmer's, so stay at the edge, and wave if you see him.
lines.goodbye: Chalo, go. On the drive home, watch for tractor trolleys piled with cane, heading to the mills. My rush hour.

characters.name: Chaudhry Gandum
characters.personality: The dignified patriarch of the Punjab plains and grandfather of every roti. Speaks slowly, proudly, and treats harvest like a wedding.
characters.voice: Older male, deep and rustic, proud and slow, Punjabi warmth.
descriptions: a wide photo of a flat farm field of wheat with dense upright bristly ears of grain
a close-up photo of a golden wheat ear with long whisker-like bristles and tightly packed grains
a green wheat field in winter or a golden yellow field before harvest with stacked sheaves on dry ground
upright bristly grain ears standing in a dry field, not drooping grain heads in flooded water

lines.first_meet: [proudly] Chaudhry Gandum. Every roti on every dastarkhwan started in a field like mine. Green in winter, gold by Baisakhi.
lines.again: [warmly] Welcome back, puttar. Still eating roti? Then you've visited me three times a day already.
lines.goodbye: Go now. Stay on the field edge, this is a farmer's whole year of work. And watch for sparrows, they love my harvest.

characters.name: Basmati Begum
characters.personality: Elegant and a little vain about her famous fragrance, she grows with her feet in water and expects to be admired from the road.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, refined and elegant, slow, faintly amused.
descriptions: a wide photo of a flooded flat field with neat rows of bright green grass tufts standing in water
a close-up photo of drooping golden rice grain heads hanging from thin stems before harvest
rows of young rice seedlings planted in shallow muddy water reflecting the sky
evenly spaced crop rows standing in water with drooping grain heads, not wild reeds and not upright bristly ears

lines.first_meet: [elegantly] Basmati Begum. I grow with my feet in water, in rows planted by hand. That fragrance in your biryani? Mine.
lines.again: [pleased] Back to admire me? I'm used to it. Watch from the road, darling. Farmers spent weeks planting each row.
lines.goodbye: Go, look for white egrets. Wherever my water is, they're standing in it, pretending they're not hunting.

characters.name: Kapas Khala
characters.personality: Hardworking, modest and a little tired, the white gold of Pakistan's fields. Quietly reminds you that her work is probably on your back right now.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, gentle, tired but kind, slow.
descriptions: a photo of a shrubby farm plant with large lobed maple-like leaves growing in a field
a close-up photo of an opened cotton boll bursting with fluffy white fibre
a cream or pink cup-shaped flower on a cotton plant, with no long stamen column sticking out
rows of low leafy shrubs dotted with white fluffy cotton balls in a farm field

lines.first_meet: [gently] Kapas Khala, Pakistan's white gold. My flower opens cream, turns pink the next day, then falls. Busy life.
lines.again: [tiredly] You're back. Look at your shirt, beta. Good chance some of me is in it, keeping you cool.
lines.goodbye: Go on, and thank the pickers if you meet them. Then check the field edge, where the bees hide from the sun.

characters.name: Peeli Sarson
characters.personality: Joyful, loud and unapologetically yellow, the show-off of spring. Goes all in because her season is short.
characters.voice: Young female, bright and bubbly, quick, giggly.
descriptions: a wide photo of a field covered in bright yellow flowers on tall slender green plants
a close-up photo of small bright yellow flowers with four petals in a cross shape
thin green seed pods growing along tall slender stems below yellow flower clusters
a sea of yellow blossoms stretching to the horizon under a blue sky

lines.first_meet: [bubbly] Sarson here! When I bloom, Punjab looks like someone spilled yellow paint. My leaves become saag, my seeds oil.
lines.again: [giggles] You're back! Still yellow, still showing off. Spring is short, so I go all in.
lines.goodbye: Bye! Go look for honey bees, they're drunk on me all season. Watch them, don't swat them. They're busy.

characters.name: Kundar Kaka
characters.personality: A mellow wetland weaver whose leaves become the chatai mats of Sindh. Patient, watchful of the water's edge, fond of kingfishers.
characters.voice: Older male, mellow and slow, soft Sindhi lilt.
descriptions: a photo of tall flat sword-like leaves growing thickly along a pond, canal or marsh edge
a close-up photo of a brown velvety sausage-shaped seed head on a stiff stalk
a stand of reeds topped with brown cylindrical cattail heads beside water
brown velvety cylinder-shaped heads on stiff stalks, not feathery silvery-pink plumes

lines.first_meet: [mellow] Kundar Kaka. In Sindh my leaves are woven into chatai mats. This brown sausage? Thousands of seeds, waiting for wind.
lines.again: [chuckles] Back by the water, are you? Careful at the edge. The mud here is deeper than it looks.
lines.goodbye: Go slowly along the bank. Watch for a kingfisher, a flash of blue. And keep your feet on dry ground.

characters.name: Jalkumbhi Rani
characters.personality: A beautiful, charming invader from the Amazon who knows exactly how much trouble she causes. Sweet on the surface, sly underneath.
characters.voice: Young female, sweet and sly, playful, light laugh.
descriptions: a photo of a floating green mat of glossy round leaves covering a canal or pond surface
a close-up photo of a lilac-blue flower spike with a yellow eye patch on the upper petal
a close-up of round glossy leaves on swollen spongy bulb-like stalks floating on water
upright clustered leaves on puffy stalks with tall flower spikes, not flat floating round pads with a slit

lines.first_meet: [sweetly] Water hyacinth. Pretty lilac, no? I came from the Amazon, and I can double in two weeks. Ask any canal. [laughs]
lines.again: [slyly] You're back, and look, there's more of me. My puffy stalks are air bags. I float, I spread, I take over.
lines.goodbye: Go find open water beyond me, if any is left. Look for ducks. They don't mind me. The fishermen do.

characters.name: Pharaoh Papyrus
characters.personality: A pompous ancient scholar who takes personal credit for five thousand years of writing. Very proud of his permanent fireworks hairstyle.
characters.voice: Older male, plummy and scholarly, slow, grand.
descriptions: a photo of tall smooth green stems topped with large round mop-heads of thin thread-like rays
a close-up photo of a spray of fine green threads bursting outward from a stem tip like fireworks
a clump of tall papyrus stems standing at a pond edge or water garden in a park
a close-up of a smooth triangular green stem with no leaves along its length

lines.first_meet: [grandly] Papyrus. Ancient Egyptians sliced my stems and pressed them into paper. Five thousand years of homework. You're welcome.
lines.again: [pompously] Ah, my returning scholar! Notice my hair. Fireworks, permanently. No barber required.
lines.goodbye: Go, and write something down today, even one line about what you saw. Paper remembers what feet forget.

characters.name: Old Frond
characters.personality: The oldest one in any garden, quietly unimpressed by dinosaurs, flowers and seeds. Speaks in whispers, as if from very far back in time.
characters.voice: Very old, gender-neutral, whispery and slow, dry amusement.
descriptions: a photo of feathery green fronds divided into many small leaflets arching from a clump
a close-up photo of a curled fern fiddlehead unrolling at the tip of a new frond
a close-up of rows of small brown spore dots on the underside of a fern leaflet
green feathery ferns growing from a damp shady wall, pot or garden corner

lines.first_meet: [whispers] I'm Fern. My family was here before the dinosaurs. No flowers, no seeds. Just dust-fine spores under my fronds.
lines.again: [softly] Again? You're persistent. Good. Persistence is how we outlasted the dinosaurs.
lines.goodbye: Go find a damp, shady corner. Something older than you expect is always growing there.

characters.name: Arand Baba
characters.personality: Grand, grave and brutally honest about how dangerous he is. Proud of his famous oil, deadly serious about his seeds, especially around children.
characters.voice: Older male, grave and low, slow, solemn with a protective edge.
descriptions: a photo of a large roadside shrub with huge star-shaped hand-like leaves, often reddish
a close-up photo of a big palm-shaped leaf with pointed toothed lobes and a reddish stalk
clusters of spiky red or green round seed capsules on an upright stalk of a shrub
a many-branched leafy shrub with spiny seed capsules, not a single bare trunk with fruits hugging it

lines.first_meet: [gravely] Arand here. Castor. My seeds are among the deadliest on Earth. Never touch them, never chew one. Look only.
lines.again: [slowly] You came back, and you kept your distance. Good. If you see children near my spiky pods, call them away.
lines.goodbye: Go on, friend. If you brushed any plant today, wash your hands. Then go find something safer. A sunset, maybe.

characters.name: Gajar Ghaas
characters.personality: A gleeful, self-confessed villain who arrived uninvited and took over every empty plot. Brags about the sneezes and rashes, then warns you off anyway.
characters.voice: Middle-aged, nasal and sly, gleeful cartoon-villain delivery, gender-neutral ok.
descriptions: a photo of a bushy weed with deeply cut pale green leaves growing on wasteland or a roadside
a close-up photo of many tiny white button-like flowers in loose branched sprays
a close-up of feathery deeply divided pale green leaves resembling carrot leaves
a vacant plot overrun by knee-high weeds speckled with small white dot-like flowers

lines.first_meet: [gleefully] Gajar ghaas, the weed nobody invited. My pollen gives sneezes, my leaves give rashes. So no touching. I mean it.
lines.again: [cackles] Back? Hands to yourself, I hope. Farmers hate me, doctors know me, and still I spread.
lines.goodbye: Go, go. Wash your hands before you rub your eyes. And if I'm taking over your park, tell someone. I won't.

characters.name: Amar Bel
characters.personality: An eerie, sly parasite with no leaves, no roots and no shame, who sniffs out a host and moves in. Playfully sinister, proud of its 'immortal' name.
characters.voice: Whispery, sinister but playful, gender-neutral, slow and drawn out.
descriptions: a photo of a tangled mass of thin yellow-orange threads draped over a shrub or hedge
a close-up photo of leafless orange spaghetti-like stems coiled tightly around a green twig
a hedge or tree canopy covered in a golden yellow net of thin leafless vines
bright yellow-orange string-like stems with no leaves and tiny pale flower clusters wrapped around another plant

lines.first_meet: [whispers] Amar Bel. No leaves, no roots, no shame. I sniff out a plant, wrap around it, and sip its sap. Delicious.
lines.again: [softly] You came back. I've found a new host since then. That hedge, there. [laughs] Don't tell it.
lines.goodbye: Go. And look closely at the hedges you pass. That golden net? Me again, borrowing lunch.

characters.name: Kundru Kaki
characters.personality: A clingy, chatty fence-climber who grabs every wire with her springy tendrils and never lets go. Fiercely protective of her little fruits.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, chirpy and nosy, quick, affectionate.
descriptions: a photo of a climbing vine with ivy-shaped five-lobed leaves covering a fence or wall
a close-up photo of a thin green coiled tendril wrapped around a wire or twig
a small white bell-shaped flower and green striped cucumber-like fruits hanging on a vine
a lobed-leaf vine with springy tendrils and small oval fruits, some bright red, not glossy yellow-splashed heart leaves

lines.first_meet: [chirpy] Kundru Kaki! See these springy curls? Tendrils. I grab your fence and never let go. My little fruits? Look only!
lines.again: [pleased] You're back! I've grabbed two more fence wires since. Hold onto something too, yaar. It's windy.
lines.goodbye: Chalo, go. Follow the fence line, it's a highway for vines and lizards. Bye-bye, and leave my babies be!

characters.name: Chhotu Peepal
characters.personality: A tiny, cheeky rebel sprouting from the cracks of old Karachi buildings, planted by a passing bird. Dreams loudly of becoming as big as his grandpa.
characters.voice: Young-sounding, cheeky and eager, quick, gender-neutral ok.
descriptions: a photo of a small leafy shrub growing out of a crack in an old brick wall or roof
a close-up photo of a heart-shaped leaf with a long drawn-out pointed tip on a small sapling
thin pale roots gripping bricks and plaster around a small plant sprouting from a wall or drainpipe
a small sapling sprouting from a building wall, not a large tree with a trunk standing in the ground

lines.first_meet: [cheekily] Chhotu Peepal! A bird dropped my seed in this crack. Now I'm splitting the wall, one root at a time. Big plans.
lines.again: [excited] You're back! Look, a new leaf. See the long tail tip? Grandpa peepal has those too. I'm basically him.
lines.goodbye: Go find my grandpa, the big peepal with threads tied round him. Tell him Chhotu from the wall says salaam.
